ownership_decision.invariant: An export writes a server setting only for a listed MCP tool its Skill declares, at a single https address with no credentials or fragment, and never a local command.

boundary_decision.interaction: packaging is handed the offered MCP tools with each Skill Version it reads, as the trial run is; it imports nothing from the context that owns the tool list.

domain_forces: The operator's MCP tool list names each listed tool's server and https address; a Skill declares tools as mcp__<server>__<tool> in allowed-tools.
Agent Plugins 1.0.0 lets a plugin carry mcp.json with remote servers; an Agent Skill cannot carry server settings.
The platform must not choose what runs on the reader's machine.
implementation_design.decision: The version read returns the offered MCP tools; mcpNeedsOf groups the declared references into declarable servers and gaps; a plugin writes mcp.json and .mcp.json for the servers and its README names servers and gaps; a single Skill package's INSTALL.md names both.
invariants_preserved: Every member still passes the single-Skill release checks and the first blocked one stops the plugin.
A member version of another Skill is still answered not found.
No local command is ever written; only remote addresses.
rejected_alternatives: Writing stdio commands, which would make the platform choose a process to run on the reader's machine.
Guessing a server for a tool not on the list.
Adding a reader field to the packaging service, which the architecture budget holds.
implementation_design.counterfactual_check: Letting an address with credentials through declarableServerURL makes the credentials row of TestDeclaredMCPToolsAreGroupedByTheServerThatProvidesThem fail.

record.statement: An export names every MCP server its Skills declare in allowed-tools that is on the operator's MCP tool list: a plugin declares each one as a remote Streamable HTTP server in mcp.json and .mcp.json, a single Skill package lists them in INSTALL.md; a tool not on the list, a server listed under two addresses, or an address with credentials or a fragment is named for the reader to set up and never written, and an export whose tool list cannot be read is not produced.
examples: A member declares mcp__docs__search and docs is listed at https://docs.example.com/mcp: mcp.json declares docs as streamable-http at that address and .mcp.json as http.
A member declares mcp__crm__lookup, which is not on the list: no server is written for it and the README names it for the reader to set up.
The MCP tool list cannot be read: no plugin is built.

record.statement: A plugin package of several Skill Versions is built only if every member passes the same release checks as a single Skill; the first blocked member stops it and is named in the refusal.
examples: Two members, the second taken down: no plugin is built and the message starts with the second member's name.
Every member releasable: a zip with plugin.json and skills/<name>/ folders is built and its shape is re-read before it is stored.

record.statement: A plugin member whose version belongs to another Skill is answered not found, so one Skill's gates never apply to another's content.
examples: A member naming skill A with a version of skill B is not found.
